3. A quantitative sufficient interface for a constant energy gap

I obtained the following operator lemma. It makes one possible composition route precise without assuming that its missing test already exists.

Gap-transfer lemma.
Suppose

 $A\succeq g(I-P),\qquad 0\preceq B\preceq I,\qquad
PBP\succeq\beta P,$ where  $g,\beta>0$ . Then

 $\boxed{
A+B\succeq\frac{g\beta}{g+1+\beta}\,I.
}                                                   \tag{4}$ 

Proof

For a unit vector  $\psi$ , put

 $v=\|(I-P)\psi\|^2,\qquad b=\langle\psi,B\psi\rangle.$ The compression assumption and triangle inequality imply

 $\sqrt{\beta}\sqrt{1-v}
\le \|B^{1/2}P\psi\|
\le \sqrt b+\sqrt v.$ Write  $E=b+gv$ . Weighted Cauchy–Schwarz gives

 $\beta(1-v)\le(\sqrt b+\sqrt v)^2
\le E(1+1/g).$ Also  $v\le E/g$ . Consequently

 $\beta\le E\frac{g+1+\beta}{g}.$ Since  $\langle\psi,(A+B)\psi\rangle\ge E$ , equation (4) follows.

Application to the code

Take

 $P=P_r,\qquad g=\frac{\sigma(r+1)}N.$ If an actual bounded-locality computation test  $B$  were constructed such that, on NO instances,

 $P_rBP_r\succeq\beta P_r                              \tag{5}$ for a fixed positive  $\beta$ , then

 $\lambda_{\min}\!\left(\frac{H_{\mathrm{code}}+B}{2}\right)
\ge
\frac{g\beta}{2(g+1+\beta)}.$ With  $r=\lfloor\rho_*N\rfloor$ , the right-hand side is bounded below by a fixed positive constant. A YES state in the codespace with sufficiently small  $B$ -expectation would give the required completeness separation.

Normalization is manageable: if  $H_{\mathrm{code}}$  and  $B$  are normalized lists containing  $m_A$  and  $m_B$  terms, respectively, replicating each first-list term  $m_B$  times and each second-list term  $m_A$  times realizes their half-sum with  $2m_Am_B$  terms. The accepted rational-output conversion can then handle precision while preserving a fixed fraction of the gap.

The test  $B$  satisfying (5) has not been constructed. It would have to enforce the whole verification relation, including required initializations, against arbitrary entangled states in the relevant physical space.

A polynomial-size circuit that decodes and runs the verifier is insufficient: turning that circuit into fixed-locality constraints with constant normalized energy soundness is precisely the unresolved step.
